assemble.doc:
Turn pieces into a clean set of separate bodies (Houdini's Assemble): number them, name them, give each its own
points and a pivot, ready for ``rbd_configure``. MiniHou has no packed primitives or string attributes, so instead
of packing, each piece's faces carry the int ``piece`` and its vector ``pivot``, and the names are the detail
attribute ``piece_names``.
assemble.label: Assemble

attrib_paint.doc:
Hold painted values of one attribute on points, primitives (faces) or edges. Elements nobody painted keep the input's value of that
attribute, or the default. The painted elements are remembered by number, so they follow the geometry only while the elements upstream
keep their numbers; ones that no longer exist are ignored and counted in the detail attribute `paint_stale_<name>`. Paint it in
the 3D view (Paint mode), assign to a selection with Quick Assign, or edit cells in the spreadsheet.
attrib_paint.label: Attribute Paint
attrib_paint.keywords: paint attribute weight mask vertex colour color assign brush edit values spreadsheet

attribute_blur.doc: Laplacian smoothing of point attributes over the mesh edges (Houdini's Attribute Blur).
attribute_blur.label: Attribute Blur

attribute_create.doc: Add an attribute with a constant value (Houdini's Attribute Create).
attribute_create.label: Attribute Create

attribute_delete.doc:
Delete attributes by name or wildcard on every domain (also detail). Useful to stop an attribute reaching Blender,
e.g. delete N to let Blender compute its own normals.
attribute_delete.label: Attribute Delete

attribute_promote.doc: Move an attribute to another domain (Houdini's Attribute Promote): points <-> primitives <-> vertices -> detail.
attribute_promote.label: Attribute Promote

attribute_randomize.doc: Random values per element, or per piece with 'by' (Houdini's Attribute Randomize). Deterministic per seed.
attribute_randomize.label: Attribute Randomize

attribute_rename.doc: Rename an attribute, e.g. a Blender color attribute 'Col' to 'Cd', or 'weight' to 'pscale'.
attribute_rename.label: Attribute Rename

attribute_transfer.doc:
Copy point attributes from the nearest point of a second geometry (Houdini's Attribute Transfer, nearest-point
mode). Within max_distance the source value is taken; blend_width softens the edge. Exact nearest neighbours
(SciPy's KD-tree when installed, otherwise a numpy grid).
attribute_transfer.label: Attribute Transfer

bend.doc:
Bend, twist and taper geometry along an axis (Houdini's Bend SOP). Inside the capture region the shape
curls into an arc; beyond it, it continues straight along the bent end. N follows the deformation. With rest
geometry on the second input the capture region is measured on the rest positions, and only the displacement
they undergo is added to the first input (so animated or already-deformed points bend as they were modelled).
bend.label: Bend

bezier.doc: Editable cubic Bezier curve (see ``bezier``); with an input, the curve is added to that geometry.
bezier.label: Bezier
bezier.keywords: curve spline tangent handles control points path

blast.doc: Delete a selection of primitives or points (Houdini's Blast). Attributes and groups are compacted to match.
blast.label: Blast

blend.doc:
Morph the base shape towards one or more targets that have the same number of points (Houdini's Blend Shapes /
Blender's shape keys). Every blended attribute becomes ``base + amount * sum(weight_i * (target_i - base))``, so with
a single target and weight 1 the amount runs from the base (0) to the target (1), and several targets add their offsets.
Normals follow when ``N`` is listed; topology and everything else comes from the base.
blend.label: Blend

blender_image.doc:
A Blender image as a pixel grid: a point per pixel (row by row from the bottom left, like Blender), `Cd` and `Alpha` point
attributes for the colour, `uv`, and the grid detail attributes the heightfield nodes use. Wrangles read and write pixels, heightfield
nodes erode a height map, `image_out` sends the result back.
blender_image.label: Blender Image
blender_image.keywords: texture picture bitmap pixels height map mask read import

blender_object.doc:
A Blender object's evaluated mesh (modifiers applied), live: edit it in Blender and the graph recooks.
Native data arrives as attributes: the render UV map as `uv` and other UV maps by name (vertices), the render color
attribute as `Cd` (+ `Alpha` if not opaque), `material_index` and `sharp_face` (primitives), vertex groups as point
floats named after the group, custom normals as vertex `N`, and every other attribute under its own name. Loose
edges (an edge-only mesh) become curves.

Curves and point clouds come in as what they are: each curve is an open primitive (cyclic ones closed), sampled exactly as Blender
draws it (Bezier handles, NURBS, Catmull-Rom, poly), with `radius` and `tilt` as point attributes and curve attributes as primitive
attributes; a point cloud is points with `radius` and its attributes. An object whose evaluated geometry holds several kinds (a
mesh, curves and points from one Geometry Nodes tree) arrives as one geometry with the parts side by side.
blender_object.label: Blender Object
blender_object.keywords: read import mesh curve curves hair point cloud

boolean.doc:
Exact boolean of two closed polygon meshes (Houdini's Boolean). The result is watertight; faces keep their
attributes (vertex attributes such as uv are interpolated across cuts), cut points blend point attributes, and
faces from each input are in groups ``from_a`` / ``from_b``. Inputs must be closed and consistently wound.
boolean.label: Boolean

boolean_fracture.doc:
Break a closed mesh with other closed meshes (Houdini's Boolean Fracture): every connected body of the cutters
carves out a piece (the input intersected with it) and what no cutter touched is the remainder. The new surface of
each piece (the cutter's) is the ``inside`` group; the input's own surface is ``outside``. Pieces are closed solids, ready for
``rbd_configure``.
boolean_fracture.label: Boolean Fracture

bound.doc:
A closed box around the input (Houdini's Bound); detail attributes ``bound_min``/``bound_max``/``bound_size``
(in the box's own axes when oriented).
bound.label: Bound

box.doc: Polygon box or surface points; optional input fits an axis-aligned bounding box before rotation.
box.label: Box

bridge.doc:
Join pairs of open boundary loops with a band of faces (Houdini's Bridge): two pipe ends become one pipe, a hole
in a wall and a hole in a floor a corridor. Equal loops get quads; loops of different sizes get triangles. Loops are
paired when each is the other's nearest loop among those of other pieces (or in order); a loop with no partner is
left open.
bridge.label: Bridge

building_rules.doc:
Generate a building per strictly convex, closed XY footprint polygon.

Storeys are divided into evenly spaced bays. Windows are shallow facade panels;
balconies are slabs with three parapets. They are not Boolean openings or interiors.
Flat and pyramid roofs accept convex polygons; gable roofs require rectangles.
Primitive component: 0 wall, 1 window, 2 balcony, 3 roof, 4 foundation.
building_rules.label: Building Rules
building_rules.keywords: building footprint facade grammar storeys windows balconies roof architecture

carve.doc:
Keep a portion of each open curve by length (Houdini's Carve). Original points inside are kept exactly; the
ends are cut with interpolated attributes. Polygons pass through.
carve.label: Carve

clean.doc: Tidy geometry (Houdini's Clean): weld, remove degenerate primitives and unused points.
clean.label: Clean

clip.doc:
Cut polygons with a plane (Houdini's Clip). Cut edges get new points with interpolated attributes; faces
straddling the plane are trimmed, not deleted. Use polyfill to cap the opening.
clip.label: Clip

color.doc: Set Cd (Houdini's Color SOP). Blender shows it as the color attribute 'Color'.
color.label: Color

connectivity.doc:
Number the connected pieces 0, 1, 2... (Houdini's Connectivity): faces sharing points are one piece. Use it
with attribute_randomize 'by', blast, or for_each.
connectivity.label: Connectivity

contour.doc:
Iso-lines or a cut surface of a point attribute over a mesh (marching squares and marching triangles in one node).
Lines carry the point attributes interpolated, a point attribute and a primitive attribute 'level'. Surface mode keeps the
polygons whole where it can and cuts them exactly on the level elsewhere.
contour.label: Contour
contour.keywords: isolines iso lines marching squares triangles topographic threshold cut surface level set

convert_line.doc: Turn every edge into curves (Houdini's Convert Line), e.g. for wireframes with sweep. Point attributes are kept.
convert_line.label: Convert Line

convex_decomposition.doc:
Cut a closed concave mesh into nearly convex pieces (Houdini's Convex Decomposition, for simulation collision shapes).
The piece with the most volume missing from its convex hull is cut next, along the plane of a face beside one of its
reflex edges (the cut that removes the most concavity wins), until every piece is within ``max_concavity`` or there are
``max_pieces``. Each cut is capped, so the pieces are closed solids; the caps are the ``inside`` group.
convex_decomposition.label: Convex Decomposition

convex_hull.doc:
The smallest convex shape holding all the input points: a closed triangle mesh facing outwards, on those of
the points that are corners of the hull (they keep their attributes). Primitives are ignored. With fewer than four
points, or points that are all in one plane, there is no volume and the points come back unchanged.
convex_hull.label: Convex Hull

copy_to_points.doc:
Stamp a copy of ``source`` on every point of ``points`` (Houdini's Copy to Points, same attributes).

Orientation, first match wins: ``orient`` (quaternion x,y,z,w), ``rot`` (Euler XYZ radians), ``N`` with ``up``
(+Z along N, +Y towards up), ``N`` alone (minimal rotation of +Z). Size: ``scale`` (per axis) times ``pscale``.
Target point attributes other than these are inherited by the copied points (overriding source attributes of
the same name); the source's N turns with each copy. Vertex, primitive and detail attributes come from
``source``.
copy_to_points.label: Copy to Points

copy_transform.doc:
Copies with an accumulating transform (Houdini's Copy and Transform): stairs, spirals, arrays. Each copy's
points get the int ``copynum``.
copy_transform.label: Copy Transform

crease.doc: Set edge creaseweight or point cornerweight for Subdivide; sharpness decays by one per level.
crease.label: Crease

curve.doc: A curve through typed-in points (Houdini's Curve SOP, as text); with an input, the curve is added to that geometry.
curve.label: Curve

curve_simplify.doc:
Fewer points on a curve with the same shape (the opposite of resample): the points that matter stay, with their attributes. Open
curves keep their ends; closed loops keep at least three points. Run it on curves (convert_line, resample, ...), not on a mesh.
curve_simplify.label: Curve Simplify
curve_simplify.keywords: decimate reduce points rdp douglas peucker fewer optimise

delaunay.doc:
Joins the points of the input into triangles so that no point lies inside any triangle's circumcircle. Only
the points are used (primitives are dropped); every point is kept with its attributes, and points that end up in
no triangle (duplicates, collinear sets) stay as loose points. Pair with ``scatter`` on a grid, or ``max_edge``
to cut a ragged outline.
delaunay.label: Delaunay

delete.doc:
Delete points matching an expression (Houdini's Blast/Delete). Primitives that use a deleted point are deleted
too; point, vertex and primitive attributes are compacted to match.
delete.label: Delete

dissolve.doc:
Merge neighbouring faces that lie in one plane (within the angle) into single n-gons, e.g. the triangles that
a boolean, a triangulate or a convex hull leave on flat sides. Points stay where they are; the merged face takes
the attributes of the lowest-numbered face of its region. Regions whose outline would pinch or enclose a hole are
left as they are.
dissolve.label: Dissolve

dissolve_edges.doc: Merge selected manifold face regions into simple n-gons. Reject holes, branches, boundary edges and seams.
dissolve_edges.label: Dissolve Edges

divide.doc:
Triangulate polygons (Houdini's Divide 'Triangulate'): convex ones as fans, concave ones by ear clipping.
Vertex and primitive attributes follow; primitive order is kept.
divide.label: Divide

edge_collapse.doc:
Merge the two ends of every selected edge into one point at their average (Houdini's Edge Collapse). Chains of
selected edges collapse to a single point; faces left with fewer than three corners disappear.
edge_collapse.label: Edge Collapse

edge_cusp.doc:
Make the selected edges look hard and everything else smooth (Houdini's Edge Cusp): writes per-corner normals
``N`` that average across every edge except the cusped ones.
edge_cusp.label: Edge Cusp

edge_flip.doc:
Swap the diagonal of the two triangles on each selected edge (Houdini's Edge Flip). Edges that are not shared by
exactly two triangles are left alone, and a triangle takes part in at most one flip.
edge_flip.label: Edge Flip

edge_group.doc: Create a derived edge group; stored as edge_group_<name> on outgoing corners for protocol compatibility.
edge_group.label: Edge Group

edge_group_promote.doc: Copy an edge selection to incident points or primitives (any selected edge). Source edge groups remain.
edge_group_promote.label: Edge Group Promote

exploded_view.doc:
Push pieces apart (Houdini's Exploded View): each moves along the line from ``center`` through its centroid.
Points shared by several pieces follow the first.
exploded_view.label: Exploded View

facet.doc:
Split shared points so each face stands alone (Houdini's Facet 'Unique Points'). Useful before moving faces
apart; for flat shading in Blender, sharp_face (a primitive int) is cheaper.
facet.label: Facet

falloff.doc:
Write a 0..1 weight (remapped to min..max) from a shape: for masks, soft selections, deformer strengths and colours. The
result is a normal float attribute that wrangles, soft_transform-like nodes, attribute_transfer and Blender all read.
falloff.label: Falloff
falloff.keywords: weight mask gradient soft selection sphere directional radial wave index distance field

fillet.doc:
Round the corners of curves with circular arcs (Houdini's Fillet). Open curves keep their end points; closed
curves and polygon outlines are rounded all the way round. Each corner becomes ``divisions + 1`` points on the arc
tangent to both segments; where two corners compete for a short segment each gets at most half of it, so arcs
never overlap. Point attributes are blended along the curve, ``curveu`` is not added. Every primitive becomes its
own curve (points are not shared afterwards).
fillet.label: Fillet

for_each.doc:
Split the geometry into pieces, run 'body' on each, merge the results. Each piece carries the detail
attributes iteration (0, 1, ...), numiterations and value (the piece's attribute value), which a wrangle inside a
system reads as @iteration etc. -- e.g. to vary a seed per piece.
for_each.label: For Each

fuse.doc:
Weld points that lie within ``distance`` of each other (snapped to a grid of that size). With a second input
the first input's points are only snapped onto the nearest point of the second (within ``distance``): the
second input is not modified, and the first input's points are not welded to each other.
fuse.label: Fuse

glue_cluster.doc:
Glue touching pieces together (Houdini's Glue Cluster). Pieces that share a cut face are linked; ``clusters`` can
merge the most firmly stuck ones into rigid groups (the int ``cluster``: configure it with ``rbd_configure`` ``compound``
on). ``output = constraints`` gives the remaining links as lines between piece centres with the attributes the solver
reads: ``rbd_a`` / ``rbd_b`` (body ids: clusters when clustering, else pieces), ``strength`` (newtons) and ``length``.
glue_cluster.label: Glue Cluster

goal_collision.doc:
Separate point spheres; packing goal, not polygon/edge self-collision.

Every pair participates, including topology neighbours. Limit: 1000 points.
goal_collision.label: Goal Collision
goal_collision.keywords: geometric constraint collision separation packing radius

goal_gravity.doc:
Apply a downward (or custom) acceleration at each relaxation step.

This is damped form-finding. Results depend on the solver timestep and iteration
count; these nodes do not replace the timeline MuJoCo RBD solver.
goal_gravity.label: Goal Gravity

goal_length.doc:
Maintain all topology edge lengths; captures rest lengths here, before relaxation.

Add diagonals to cloth if shear resistance is desired. This goal has no bending term.
goal_length.label: Goal Length
goal_length.keywords: geometric constraint edge length cable fabric

goal_pin.doc: Fix selected points at their incoming positions. Pins take precedence over other goals.
goal_pin.label: Goal Pin

goal_solve.doc:
Replay deterministic position-based geometric goals from the incoming geometry.

Chain goal nodes into this input. Topology and attributes survive except normals N,
which are removed after deformation; append a Normal node to recompute them.
Detail goal_report records residuals, displacement, steps and convergence. Incompatible
goals need not converge. No material stiffness, structural certification or cloth collision.
goal_solve.label: Goal Solve
goal_solve.keywords: geometric constraints relaxation solver goals fabric cable packing

goal_surface.doc:
Pull selected points to the closest point on a fixed triangle/polygon surface.

Target polygons use the engine's fan triangulation; use convex faces or triangulate
first. This is a two-sided attachment, not a one-sided collision obstacle.
goal_surface.label: Goal Surface

grid.doc:
Rectangular grid of quads in the XY plane. ``columns``/``rows`` count points per side.

Writes point attributes ``P`` and ``uv`` (u along X, v along Y).
grid.label: Grid

group_create.doc:
Make a named group of points, primitives or edges (stored as the int attribute group_<name>, 1 = member; edge
groups as edge_group_<name>). Most nodes take a group field, and Blender gets each group as a boolean attribute.
group_create.label: Group Create

group_expand.doc:
Grow or shrink a group by rings of neighbours (Houdini's Group Expand): select a face, expand once to get its
border ring (then subtract the original), contract to pull a selection away from open edges and holes in it.
group_expand.label: Group Expand

group_promote.doc: Convert the opposite domain to the target, replacing any same-name target group and removing the source.
group_promote.label: Group Promote

group_range.doc: Group a numeric range of points or primitives, optionally every Nth (Houdini's Group by Range).
group_range.label: Group Range

heightfield_erode.doc:
Erode a terrain grid: rivers cut valleys and lay down fans of sediment, then over-steep slopes slump. Writes
flow (river mask 0..1), erosion and deposit point attributes for shading. A second input with a 'mask' point
attribute restricts the change: the result is blended with the original terrain by the mask.
heightfield_erode.label: Heightfield Erode

helix.doc: A spiral curve around +Z (springs, vines, stair rails).
helix.label: Helix

image_file.doc:
A PNG file as a pixel grid, like `blender_image` but from disk: the way to bring in height maps and masks that came from Houdini or
any paint program.
image_file.label: Image File
image_file.keywords: png texture picture bitmap pixels height map mask load file

image_out.doc:
Send an image to Blender: the geometry passes through unchanged, and the link makes (or updates) the Blender image `image` from
the attribute `source`, optionally writing a PNG as well. Float images keep every value; `srgb` makes an 8-bit sRGB image.
image_out.label: Image Out
image_out.keywords: texture picture bitmap pixels bake export write png

input.doc:
An input of a system (a graph saved in the node folder and used as a node). Inside the system it receives what is
wired into the system node; when the system graph is opened on its own it passes ``preview`` through, so you can
build the system on stand-in geometry.
input.label: Input

inset.doc: Inset selected faces without height; amount is the perpendicular distance from the original boundary.
inset.label: Inset

instance.doc:
Turn points into instances of Blender objects: Blender's Geometry Nodes proxy places the real objects on them
(Instance on Points), so huge counts stay cheap and the objects stay editable in Blender.
instance.label: Instance

lattice.doc: Trilinear displacement from a complete axis-aligned rectilinear rest grid. Deformed controls retain point order.
lattice.label: Lattice

lattice_grid.doc: Complete 3D control-point grid for Lattice: columns X, rows Y, layers Z; X varies fastest.
lattice_grid.label: Lattice Grid

linear_taper.doc:
Scale points across an axis by an amount that blends from 1 at the origin to ``taper`` at ``length`` (Houdini's
Linear Taper); past the length the scale keeps going.
linear_taper.label: Linear Taper

loop_begin.label: Loop Begin

loop_end.doc:
Loop End: repeat the paired Begin/body region, feeding each result back internally.

Connect Begin directly to the begin pairing port, and the body's last node to geo.
Nested blocks are supported; external inputs remain unchanged during the repeat.
loop_end.label: Loop End

lsystem.doc:
Grow plants and fractals from rewriting rules (Houdini's L-System). Output: curves along the turtle's path (+Z is up)
with a width attribute, or polygon tubes; leaf points (group 'leaves') where J appears with no Leaf J input, and copies of the
Leaf J/K/M inputs at J/K/M. + / - yaw, & / ^ pitch, backslash / slash roll in the moving turtle frame. Enable Separate Angles
to control each axis independently. Branches restore the entire frame.

Differs from Houdini in these ways: + turns left and - right (the node's original convention), Rules is one multi-line box
instead of numbered fields, the meta test is the bounding box of its input rather than a metaball field, and tubes are
straight per F (Tension and Branch Blend are accepted but not used yet).
lsystem.label: L-System

match_size.doc:
Fit geometry to a target position and size (Houdini's Match Size). A second input replaces the target
position and size with its own bounding box.
match_size.label: Match Size

measure_area.doc: Measure polygon face areas and total surface area.
measure_area.label: Measure Area

measure_bounds.doc: Measure bounding box size and centre.
measure_bounds.label: Measure Bounds

measure_distance.doc: Measure Euclidean distance between two points or element groups.
measure_distance.label: Measure Distance

measure_length.doc: Measure curve or polyline length per primitive and total.
measure_length.label: Measure Length

measure_volume.doc: Measure closed-mesh volume using the divergence theorem.
measure_volume.label: Measure Volume

merge.doc: Concatenate any number of geometries. Attributes missing on an input are zero-filled.
merge.label: Merge

mirror.doc:
Reflect geometry across a plane (Houdini's Mirror). The copy's winding is reversed so it faces outwards, and N
is reflected.
mirror.label: Mirror

modifier_input.doc:
Mesh entering this MiniHou modifier at its stack position, in object coordinates.

The Rust editor may store an ordered ``modifier_inputs`` interface on this node.
Each entry has a stable id, Blender socket name and type, and a default; a
node parameter can refer to it with ``{"modifier_input":{"node":"input","id":"..."}}``.

Supplied by an independent modifier instance. This node cannot cook in the legacy proxy session.
modifier_input.label: Modifier Input

noise.doc:
Fractal Perlin noise sampled at P * frequency + offset.

Output range is roughly [-1, 1] before 'amplitude'. For ``attrib == "P"`` the result is
added to P. For other attributes it is written as a float attribute in scalar mode
(value * amplitude.x) or a vec3 in vector mode.
noise.label: Noise

normal.doc:
Compute ``N`` (unit length). Faces are counter-clockwise when seen from the side N points to.
Points not used by any face get N = (0, 0, 0). Vertex normals reach Blender as custom normals.
normal.label: Normal

null.doc: Pass the input through unchanged (Houdini's Null): a named place to read or output from.
null.label: Null

object_input.doc: Import an evaluated Blender mesh from this modifier's own object picker, in source-local coordinates.
object_input.label: Object Input

occlusion.doc:
Per-point ambient occlusion or wall thickness by ray casting: a mask for dirt, edge wear, subsurface strength, cavities,
or a 3-D-print wall check. Needs a polygon mesh; the point normals are computed (smooth) if the points have no N.
occlusion.label: Occlusion
occlusion.keywords: ambient occlusion ao thickness cavity dirt wear rays sss mask

output.doc:
Marks the geometry the live link publishes. The evaluator validates it (P present, indices in range). Give an
output an ``object`` name to publish more than one result: each named output (that is not the display node) becomes
its own mesh object in Blender.
output.label: Output

outset.doc: Offset selected planar boundaries outward, without height. Does not resolve collisions with neighbours.
outset.label: Outset

path_deform.doc:
Bend geometry along a curve (Houdini's Path Deform, Blender's Curve modifier). Cross-sections follow
rotation-minimising frames, so nothing twists unless asked; beyond the ends the geometry continues straight.
Uses the first primitive of the curve input; rotates N.
path_deform.label: Path Deform

pcg_bounds.doc: Set or scale the points' boxes (PCG's Bounds Modifier): what the booleans and self-pruning test.
pcg_bounds.label: PCG Bounds

pcg_copy_points.doc:
Copy a set of points onto every target point, composing their transforms (PCG's Copy Points): clusters,
rings of rocks around each tree... Seeds mix both, densities multiply.
pcg_copy_points.label: PCG Copy Points

pcg_debug.doc: Show each point as its box (PCG's Debug view), to see what the booleans and pruning see.
pcg_debug.label: PCG Debug

pcg_density_filter.doc: Keep points by density (PCG's Density Filter).
pcg_density_filter.label: PCG Density Filter

pcg_density_noise.doc:
Vary density with noise (PCG's Density Noise / Spatial Noise): feed a density filter to thin points in
patches.
pcg_density_noise.label: PCG Density Noise

pcg_difference.doc:
Remove points whose boxes overlap the other input (PCG's Difference): its points' boxes, or the inside of a
closed mesh (a house footprint, a road made with sweep...).
pcg_difference.label: PCG Difference

pcg_distance.doc: Density from the distance to another input: a mesh's surface, a curve, or its points (PCG's Distance).
pcg_distance.label: PCG Distance

pcg_intersection.doc:
Keep points whose boxes overlap the other input (PCG's Intersection): its points' boxes, or the inside of
a closed mesh.
pcg_intersection.label: PCG Intersection

pcg_points.doc:
Turn any points (a mesh's, a scatter's...) into PCG points: fills rot, scale, bounds, density and seed where
missing and drops the primitives.
pcg_points.label: PCG Points

pcg_projection.doc: Drop points onto a surface (PCG's Projection): terrain, a roof, a wall...
pcg_projection.label: PCG Projection

pcg_self_prune.doc: Remove points whose boxes overlap others (PCG's Self Pruning): no two remaining boxes overlap.
pcg_self_prune.label: PCG Self Prune

pcg_spawner.doc:
Choose a Blender object for every point by weight (PCG's Static Mesh Spawner); Blender instances them with
each point's rot and scale. Also writes ``variant`` (0-based choice) for copy_to_points or wrangles.
pcg_spawner.label: PCG Spawner

pcg_spline_sampler.doc:
Points along curves, their X axis following the curve (PCG's Spline Sampler), or on a grid inside closed
curves.
pcg_spline_sampler.label: PCG Spline Sampler

pcg_surface_sampler.doc:
Points on a surface (PCG's Surface Sampler): random positions thinned to an even spacing, with N, bounds,
density 1 and a per-point seed.
pcg_surface_sampler.label: PCG Surface Sampler

pcg_transform.doc: Random offsets, rotations and scales per point (PCG's Transform Points), driven by each point's seed.
pcg_transform.label: PCG Transform

pcg_union.doc: Merge point sets (PCG's Union), optionally combining the density where they overlap.
pcg_union.label: PCG Union

pcg_volume_sampler.doc: Points on a grid inside a closed mesh (PCG's Volume Sampler); each point's box is its voxel.
pcg_volume_sampler.label: PCG Volume Sampler

peak.doc:
Move points along their normals (Houdini's Peak): inflate, shrink or offset a surface. Uses N if present,
else area-weighted point normals.
peak.label: Peak

point.doc: Create one editable point, with no edges or faces. Useful as a copy target or graph seed.
point.label: Point

point_deform.doc: Weighted local affine displacement fit to corresponding control clouds. NumPy-only; no stored capture or piece matching.
point_deform.label: Point Deform

point_jitter.doc: Move points by a random offset (Houdini's Point Jitter).
point_jitter.label: Point Jitter

point_relax.doc:
Push points apart to an even spacing and keep them on the surface (Houdini's Point Relax / Scatter's relax
iterations): turns clumpy random scatter into blue-noise-like distributions.
point_relax.label: Point Relax

points_to_surface.doc: A smooth surface around points (VDB from Particles / metaballs): blobs, liquids, organic shapes.
points_to_surface.label: Points to Surface

polybevel.doc:
Bevel polygon edges with segmented round or flat profiles. Keep ``distance`` below half
the shortest bevelled face edge, or the cuts overlap. N is removed (recompute it with a normal node).
polybevel.label: PolyBevel

polybridge.doc: Linear quad bridge between equal-size boundary chains/loops. No unequal resampling or intersection repair.
polybridge.label: PolyBridge

polyexpand2d.doc: Offset independent convex closed planar loops in their own planes. Reject concavity, holes/union requests and collapse.
polyexpand2d.label: PolyExpand2D

polyextrude.doc:
Extrude faces along their normals with optional inset (Houdini's PolyExtrude). Side walls are added on the
region's boundary; groups extrudeFront and extrudeSide hold the new faces.
polyextrude.label: PolyExtrude

polyfill.doc:
Close every hole with one n-gon facing the same way as its surroundings (Houdini's PolyFill, single polygon).
New faces get zero for primitive and vertex attributes.
polyfill.label: PolyFill

polypath.doc: Join curves that share end points into single polylines (Houdini's PolyPath). Polygons pass through.
polypath.label: PolyPath

polyreduce.doc:
Reduce the polygon count while keeping the shape (Houdini's PolyReduce, quadric error metrics). Point
attributes blend along each collapsed edge (others follow the kept point); vertex attributes follow their
corners. Output: triangles.
polyreduce.label: PolyReduce

polysplit.doc:
Insert edge loops or cut faces (Houdini's PolySplit). A loop runs through connected quads on both sides of the
chosen edge until it meets a boundary or a face that is not a quad; that face gets the new point too, so there are
no cracks.
polysplit.label: PolySplit

pushpull.doc:
Push/pull a single planar convex face with solid union/subtraction. Closed meshes only.
Unlike ordinary extrusion, an inward pull removes intersected solid and can punch through.
Unsupported or non-manifold results fail clearly rather than returning broken geometry.
pushpull.label: Push / Pull

python.doc:
Run Python on the geometry you wire in (numpy as np, Geometry, groups). Variables a b c d i j v s flag, any named
values from Variables, Frame/Time/TimeInc and the inputs geo, input1..3 are in scope; set `out` to the result (a
Geometry, or an (n, 3) array of points), or leave it out to pass `geo` through. Inputs are read-only: copy before
editing. Disabled unless the engine runs with --allow-python (or MINIHOU_PYTHON_NODES=1), because a graph file can then
run code; treat the node as a pure function of its inputs and parameters (results are cached).
python.label: Python

ray.doc:
Project points onto the target: along a direction, along their normals, or to the closest point. Writes
hitdist (-1 on a miss), hitprim (-1), hitN (the target's face normal) and the group rayHit.
ray.label: Ray

rbd_configure.doc:
Configure closed convex polygon pieces; keep all render geometry and attributes intact.

Primitive rbd_* attributes can subsequently be edited per piece with a wrangle.
Geometry positions define the initial pose; use Transform before configuring.
rbd_configure.label: RBD Configure

rbd_constraint.doc:
Create one physical link. Merge several links into RBD Solver's constraints input.

This is constraint geometry, not simulated render geometry. Pin is a ball joint (three
free rotations); hinge has one free rotation. All anchors use the initial scene pose.
rbd_constraint.label: RBD Constraint
rbd_constraint.keywords: hinge spring pin glue joint anchor tendon limits break physics

rbd_constraint_properties.doc:
Edit the glue links of ``glue_cluster`` (Houdini's RBD Constraint Properties): set or scale the break strength of a
group of links, with random variation, or make them unbreakable. Chain several to give different parts of a structure
different strengths.
rbd_constraint_properties.label: RBD Constraint Properties

rbd_material_fracture.doc:
A one-node fracture for simulation (Houdini's RBD Material Fracture): scatter fracture points, cut the closed
mesh with ``voronoi_fracture`` (again for each further ``fracture_level``), give each piece its own points, glue the
pieces and set mass (density x volume), friction and bounce from the material. Feed ``output = pieces`` to
``rbd_solver`` and ``output = constraints`` to its third input. Pieces are convex when the input is; for a concave
input switch on ``convex_parts`` (each concave piece becomes a compound body of convex parts).
rbd_material_fracture.label: RBD Material Fracture

rbd_solver.doc:
Simulate convex rigid pieces with body-body contacts using optional MuJoCo 3.15.0.

Static geometry only. Integer frames are solved with fixed substeps; fractional frames
hold the preceding integer frame. One unit = one metre. All inputs share one space.

``constraints``: merge links from RBD Constraint or Glue Cluster. Glue welds, ball pins,
limited hinges and axial springs are supported. Body IDs come from RBD Configure.
See docs/RBD-CONSTRAINTS.md for mechanisms, units, limits and break semantics.
rbd_solver.label: RBD Solver

region_identify.doc:
Label connected polygon regions; sharing any point joins a region.

Primitive mode separates each face (useful for paving). Attribute mode uses existing
integer labels. Writes region_id, region_random, region_center and region Cd.
region_identify.label: Region Identify
region_identify.keywords: connected islands regions flood fill connectivity

region_transform.doc:
Independently transform/extrude labelled regions, splitting shared boundaries.

Reuses connected PolyExtrude, so a connected multi-face patch has walls only along
its outer boundary. Without region_id, connected components are identified first.
Extrusion is performed before the centroid transform, with the original backs kept.
region_transform.label: Region Transform
region_transform.keywords: regions islands random rotate scale extrude paving tiles stones damage

remesh.doc:
Voxel remesh a closed mesh into an even, watertight quad mesh (VDB from Polygons -> smooth -> convert):
merges overlapping parts, closes small gaps, optional offset and smoothing. Needs closed meshes.
remesh.label: Remesh

resample.doc:
Even spacing along curves (Houdini's Resample). Closed polygons are resampled along their outline. Adds
curveu (0 at the start, 1 at the end) for ramps, carve and sweep.
resample.label: Resample

reverse.doc: Reverse the winding of primitives, which flips the side they face (Houdini's Reverse).
reverse.label: Reverse

revolve.doc:
Spin curves (or polygon outlines) around an axis into a surface (Houdini's Revolve): a profile of a vase, a wheel
or a goblet becomes the solid. Each segment of a profile makes a ring of quads; points on the axis are shared, so a
profile that runs from the axis to the axis gives a closed shell with triangles at the poles. Writes corner `uv`
(u around the axis, v along the profile by length); point attributes follow their points, primitive attributes
their profile.
revolve.label: Revolve

scatter.doc:
Scatter points uniformly over the surface (area weighted), or inside a closed mesh.

Output is a point cloud with ``P``, ``N`` (face normal; zero in volume mode) and ``primnum`` (source primitive;
-1 in volume mode). Primitives are fan-triangulated for sampling. An input with no area yields an empty cloud.
Uses a Numba kernel when available; the numpy path draws the same random numbers in the same order.
scatter.label: Scatter

scene_objects.doc:
Make Blender objects out of points. The geometry passes through unchanged; what happens in Blender is described by the
manifest the link sends (see the manual). Objects are never deleted by a cook: ones that are no longer needed are hidden, and
a Clean up button in the MiniHou panel removes them for good.
scene_objects.label: Scene Objects
scene_objects.keywords: realize real objects scene export blender instances scatter

sdf_boolean.doc:
Boolean of two closed meshes through distance fields: robust (no fragile intersection math), watertight, with
optional smooth fillets; edges are as sharp as the voxel size allows.
sdf_boolean.label: SDF Boolean

sdf_shape.doc:
An analytic shape as a watertight quad mesh (Higgsas' SDF nodes): sphere, box, cylinder, capsule, ellipsoid, torus,
round cone and n-sided prism, with rounded edges, a position and a rotation. Feed several through sdf_boolean for smooth
unions and subtractions.
sdf_shape.label: SDF Shape
sdf_shape.keywords: signed distance primitive sphere box capsule torus cylinder cone prism metaball implicit

set_material.doc:
Assign materials by name (Houdini's Material SOP). Faces keep their `material_index`; the name list that gives the numbers
their meaning travels with the geometry, through merges and booleans, into Blender's material slots and USD's material
bindings. To give every piece of a fracture its own material, set `index_attrib` to the piece attribute and list names; to give
Scene Objects instances their own, use the points domain.
set_material.label: Set Material

skin.doc:
Stretch a surface across a row of curves (Houdini's Skin / loft): every curve is resampled to the same number
of points by arclength and consecutive curves are joined with quads, in primitive order. Closed curves give
tubes (closed in the other direction too with `loop`). Writes `uv` (u along the curves, v across them).
skin.label: Skin

skin_profiles.doc: Loft quads through multiple ordered polygon/polyline profiles. Correspondence is by corner index, without resampling.
skin_profiles.label: Skin Profiles

slice.doc:
Cut a mesh with parallel planes into curves (topographic lines, layer outlines, cross-sections). Writes the point
attribute and primitive attribute 'level' (height above the origin plane along the normal).
slice.label: Slice
slice.keywords: cross section planes layers topographic outline 3d print contour

smooth.doc:
Smooth the shape (Houdini's Smooth). Taubin's lambda|mu filter removes noise without shrinking; N is
recomputed if present.
smooth.label: Smooth

soft_peak.doc:
Peak with a soft edge (Houdini's Soft Peak): the group moves along its normals by ``distance``, points within
``radius`` of it follow by a falling-off share. Falloff is straight-line distance.
soft_peak.label: Soft Peak

soft_transform.doc: Transform with radial smoothstep/linear falloff. No geodesic distance or selection-centred multi-source capture.
soft_transform.label: Soft Transform

solidify.doc:
Make a polygon surface into a solid shell of constant thickness: the original faces, a copy offset along the normals with
the opposite winding, and a rim of quads along every open edge. Closed meshes become a hollow shell (two nested surfaces).
Attributes ride along (points and corners copied to the inner surface; the rim takes those of the face it closes);
N is removed. Curves in the input pass through untouched.
solidify.label: Solidify
solidify.keywords: thickness shell thicken wall modifier hollow

solver.doc:
Run 'body' on the previous frame's result, frame after frame, from start_frame to the current frame (Houdini's
Solver). Deterministic: any frame gives the same result however you got there; playback is incremental (recent
frames are remembered), jumping ahead steps from the nearest remembered frame, and going back before it restarts
from the input. Inside the body, @Frame is the frame being solved and @TimeInc the step in seconds.
solver.label: Solver

sort.doc:
Reorder points or primitives (Houdini's Sort): changes @ptnum / @primnum order, which matters for copies,
ids and anything indexed by number. Topology and attributes are kept consistent.
sort.label: Sort

sphere.doc: UV sphere: triangle fans at the poles, quads between; outward-facing, closed.
sphere.label: Sphere

squash_stretch.doc: Scale along an axis and (optionally) compensate across it (Houdini's Squash and Stretch).
squash_stretch.label: Squash Stretch

subdivide.doc:
Subdivide polygons into quads (Houdini's Subdivide). Catmull-Clark smooths towards a limit surface and keeps open
boundaries as smooth curves; linear splits without moving anything. Faces with fewer than 3 points are dropped.
subdivide.label: Subdivide

sweep.doc:
Tubes along curves (Houdini's Sweep / PolyWire): rotation-minimising frames (no flips), radius scaled by
point width or pscale, uv along (u) and around (v) the tube, curve point attributes kept on the rings.
Closed primitives (closed curves, polygon outlines) make closed rings. A second input replaces the circle with
its own cross-section (open sections make open sheets, closed ones tubes with caps).
sweep.label: Sweep

switch.doc: Pass on one of several inputs (Houdini's Switch): try variants, or expose the choice as a parameter.
switch.label: Switch

torus.doc: Torus in the XY plane (Houdini's Torus), outward-facing quads with vertex uvs; closed.
torus.label: Torus

transform.doc: Scale, then rotate, then translate about ``pivot``. Also rotates ``N`` if present.
transform.label: Transform

tube.doc: Cylinder or cone along +Z (Houdini's Tube), outward-facing, with vertex uvs; closed when ``caps`` is on.
tube.label: Tube

twist.doc: Rotate points about an axis by an angle that grows with the distance along it (Houdini's Twist).
twist.label: Twist

usd_export.doc:
Passes its input on unchanged; its **Save to Disk** button writes the cooked geometry to a USD file (always at full size, whatever the
proxy level). Settings: format (binary or text), the root prim, the current frame or a frame range (an animation), up axis, units,
whether materials and the graph are written. Houdini,
Blender, Maya and usdview open the result; a file written here reads back through `usd_import` with its points, groups and details.
usd_export.label: USD Export
usd_export.keywords: usd usda usdc save write export file scene pixar omniverse houdini rop

usd_import.doc:
Meshes, curves and points of a USD file, in world space, merged into one geometry: the file's own transforms are applied,
primvars become attributes (`st` as `uv`, `displayColor` as `Cd`, normals as `N`, others by name), GeomSubsets become groups, and a
file exported by MiniHou comes back with its point order, groups and detail attributes. Other prim types (cubes, spheres, ...) are
skipped and listed in the detail attribute `usd_skipped`. Needs the usd-core package (pip install usd-core).

Settings follow Houdini's USD Import where MiniHou has the same idea: file (with a picker), Reload, time offset and scale, what to do
with a missing file, a Primitives pattern, purposes and a path attribute. Variants, traversal, display as, pivot and unpack have no
counterpart: MiniHou reads the geometry, not the stage.
usd_import.label: USD Import
usd_import.keywords: usd usda usdc usdz open load file scene pixar omniverse houdini

uv_flatten.doc:
Unwrap UVs with least-squares conformal maps (Houdini's UV Flatten): low-distortion islands cut at sharp edges
(closed shapes are cut automatically), scaled to keep their relative size and packed into 0-1. Writes vertex
``uv`` (Blender's 'UVMap').
uv_flatten.label: UV Flatten

uv_project.doc: Project texture coordinates onto the geometry (written as vertex uv, Blender's UV map).
uv_project.label: UV Project

uv_transform.doc:
Move, rotate, scale, flip and randomise texture coordinates, all together or per island or face, optionally lining a 3-D direction
up with a uv axis first. Writes the result as face-corner uv (the attribute named in `uv`).
uv_transform.label: UV Transform
uv_transform.keywords: texture coordinates move rotate scale flip mirror island randomise offset align

voronoi_adjacency.doc:
Which pieces touch (Houdini's Voronoi Adjacency): a point at each piece's centre (or at the matching point of the
second input, numbered by the piece) and a two-point curve between pieces that share a cut face. Prim attributes: ``piece_a``,
``piece_b`` and ``area`` (the contact area); points carry ``piece`` and the number of ``neighbors``.
voronoi_adjacency.label: Voronoi Adjacency

voronoi_fracture.doc:
Break a closed polygon mesh into the Voronoi cells of the ``points`` input (e.g. scattered inside it). Pieces
are closed meshes sharing their cut faces; give each a different transform or hand them to a simulation.
voronoi_fracture.label: Voronoi Fracture

voronoi_fracture_points.doc:
Fracture points for ``voronoi_fracture`` (Houdini's Voronoi Fracture Points): scattered inside a closed mesh, with
optional surface points, thinning, relaxation, clustering and points from a second input. Connect the result to
the fracture's second input.
voronoi_fracture_points.label: Voronoi Fracture Points

voronoi_split.doc:
Split any polygon geometry (open sheets, soup, solids) by the Voronoi cells of the ``points`` input (Houdini's
Voronoi Split): faces are cut where they cross a bisector plane and nothing is capped, so each piece keeps only
the surface that was already there. Use it on thin or open geometry, ``voronoi_fracture`` on solids.
voronoi_split.label: Voronoi Split

wrangle.doc:
Attribute wrangle: run a snippet over points, primitives or vertices (compiled once per snippet, numpy speed).
Reads attributes of other domains (promoted), writes to the domain it runs over; uv, Cd, N, material_index and
sharp_face arrive in Blender as UV map, color attribute, normals, material index and flat shading. Groups are
@group_<name> ints: writing i@group_top = @P.z > 1 makes a group. The extra inputs are read with @opinput1_<name>
(same element number) and @near1_<name> (nearest point).
wrangle.label: Wrangle

scatteralign.doc: Scatter points over a surface with normal alignment, random rotation, scale, and copied point attributes. Volume mode uses the legacy scatter sampler.
scatteralign.label: Scatter and Align
